title: Bramble and Starry's Light Path
markdown:
Once upon a time, Bramble the bunny lived in a green meadow that smelled of warm grass. His fur was brown and soft. His whiskers wiggled when he found something new. Starry the teddy bear was his best friend. Starry was yellow and fluffy, like a little cloud with two shiny button eyes.

Every day, Bramble and Starry played until their paws and paws-of-stuffing felt happily tired. Bramble hopped after butterflies whose wings looked like tiny painted sails. Starry watched with his kind button eyes. When they were worn out, they held pretend tea parties. They lifted pretend cups. They sipped pretend tea made of dandelion puffs, and the puffs tickled their noses until they giggled and giggled.

Until one day, the very last butterfly flew away. It had bright blue wings. It sailed over the tall grass and into the big sky. The meadow turned a soft purple, like a sleepy hug. The crickets began their night song. Bramble’s whiskers drooped. The meadow looked bigger now. The light was going away fast. He did not know which way to hop. He wiggled his nose. It did not feel like playtime anymore.

Because of that, Starry snuggled close. Starry always listened with his fluffy ears. He gave Bramble a warm squeeze that said, without any words at all, I am here with you. Bramble leaned into the hug. His ears still listened for the lost butterfly, but they listened for Starry too.

Because of that, something surprising happened by Bramble’s paws. Little lights began to glow. They were not bright. They were gentle, like tiny stars saying hello from the grass. They blinked on, one by one. They made a soft friendly path past the sleepy buttercups and around the rustling ferns. The air smelled sweet, like dirt after rain and flowers that open at night.

Until finally, Bramble nudged Starry, and they followed those slow kind lights. The lights danced like friendly fireflies. They led the friends to a big log covered in moss, as round and kind as a giant’s shoulder. Around the log, other friends were already tucked in. Finley the field mouse slept in a bed of leaves. Pip the robin tucked his head under his wing on a twig. Everyone breathed softly. The log felt warm. The air smelled of moss and honey flowers.

Ever since then, when the sun yawns and the trees whisper as the sky grows dark, Bramble and Starry look for the little lights in the grass. The meadow still turns purple. The last butterfly still flies home. And the blinking path still leads them, paw by paw, to the mossy log where night feels safe.
